text:
[RFCS.21.1] A `ComputationError` atom records a **trap** — a computation with no honest
answer ([LERR.1.4.1]). Its body is `proto/engine_error.proto#ComputationError`, and
it is the first of the two steps [LERR.9.1] orders: **record the event, then
assert the fault fact.** Recording is the delivery: the integrator receives the
atom on the stream callback ([NCBK.2.8]), and no separate fault callback
follows. The fault fact is itself recorded, as a `FactEmit` ([LERR.9.8]). A trap that is not
recorded did not happen as far as any consumer can tell.

**Container-legality `stream`, stream-class `compare`** (field 325). It is
provenance in exactly the sense `CallIssued` and `RuleFireAnnotation` are: a
replayer compares it.

**Identity is `rule_name` + `timetag`**, the same pair `CallIssued` and
`RuleFireAnnotation` carry ([RFCS.15]), so a trap joins to the activation that
caused it with no new join key.

**A trap raised while matching carries `timetag` 0.** No activation exists
then ([LERR.9.11]), and the engine **must not** give any activation the timetag
0, so 0 names no activation. Such a trap is told apart by its `rule_name`
(`$beta_<id>`), `node_id` and `fact_id`, and placed among one operation's
traps by [LERR.1.4.12].

**The slot-context fields name the offending operand** ([LERR.9.12]): set when
that operand is a slot read, and absent otherwise. Every kind this atom records
is a **computation** error ([LERR.1.4.9]). A resource limit is a `BoundsError` or
an `EngineError`, and is not recorded here; a recorder failure is no fault at
all ([NCBK.1.5]).

**`recoverable` is carried on the wire and is not derivable from `kind`.**
[LERR.1.4.9] makes recoverability a property of the occurrence rather than of
the kind: the test is whether engine state is still trustworthy. Every kind this
atom records is `reported`.

**A recorder failure is not this atom's concern.** The recorder is a **hook
layer**, not a writer (RARC.5.8, [IARC.1.14] — libds writes no file), so the
engine emits the record as it emits any other and it is the **integrator's
sink** that may be unable to persist it (RARC.5.8.13). A failing sink's status is
what the call that fired the callback returns ([NCBK.1.5]), and the engine does
not halt.

---

alloy.name: rfcs_21_1__ans
alloy.note: Filters in source order, then the rest in the order: how it ended. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

alloy.name: rfcs_21_1__body
alloy.note: The body of the atom a fault records -- every recorded field after the kind, recording provenance excluded -- totally ordered.

alloy.name: rfcs_21_1__rec
alloy.note: M1: the atom recorded -- a fault a filter raised, else the best fault when nothing false stopped it. [LERR.1.4.11]: only the fault the expression yields reaches a surface -- recorded ([RFCS.21.1]), delivered to a callback or counted -- and the model's record stands for all three. Recording every evaluated fault (M2) is not order independent (`gap__m2_order_dependent`, a counterexample tied to no clause).

alloy.name: rfcs_21_1__v5_one_atom
alloy.note: ONE ATOM: kind then body is total over what is recorded, so at most one atom is recorded. Kind alone breaks it (TEETH). [LERR.1.4.11]: only the fault the expression yields reaches a surface -- recorded ([RFCS.21.1]), delivered to a callback or counted -- and the model's record stands for all three. Recording every evaluated fault (M2) is not order independent (`gap__m2_order_dependent`, a counterexample tied to no clause).

alloy.name: rfcs_21_1__v5_selfjoin
alloy.note: THE SELF-JOIN: two traps of one kind over two facts; every order records the lesser body.
